text:
Calgary lost 6-1, but for the first 20 minutes it played like the better team. The Flames carried 0.93 expected goals to Seattle's 0.44 in the first period and still trailed 3-0, because the Kraken scored on three chances that were rated at 20, 2 and 4 percent. Jordan Eberle cashed in on the power play at 9:10, Vince Dunn fired a slap shot past Dustin Wolf 32 seconds later, and Frederick Gaudreau added one with 30 seconds left in the period.

The game turned in the second, when Seattle outchanced Calgary 1.44 to 0.87, and the third was lopsided, 1.85 to 0.73. Chandler Stephenson (backhand) and Matty Beniers (slap shot) scored 51 seconds apart early in the third to make it 5-0. Seattle ended up at 3.73 expected goals to Calgary's 2.53, and Wolf allowed exactly that many, finishing 2.27 goals worse than expected. At the other end, Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 25 shots and finished 1.53 goals better than expected. Calgary also took 12 penalty minutes to Seattle's 4.

Six goals flatters the Kraken a little. A replay of every shot has them winning 69 percent of the time, a clear edge but not a rout, and Calgary had the better of the shot attempts, 64 to 59. Ryan Strome broke the shutout at 16:35 of the third, and Kaapo Kakko answered 26 seconds later. Dunn finished with a goal and two assists in 20:36 of ice time, and Jared McCann added three assists.
